Where to Stay in Uthai Thani?

heroSub: 10 hand-picked Uthai Thani hotels across every budget — a lotus-pond garden homestay in the town centre, a garden-bungalow resort in Thap Than, riverside stays on the Sakae Krang, a resort with a pool, and a floating raft house. Covering the town centre, the riverside and the suburbs. From roughly ฿650–1,200/night.
introH2: 🪷 Why does choosing the right area in Uthai Thani matter so much?
introHtml: Uthai Thani is a small, quiet town on the Sakae Krang River that many people come to for a weekend — to wander the riverside morning market, cycle along the river and climb Khao Sakae Krang to pay respects at the temple. Stays fall into three sides with very different feels — the town centre (Uthai Mai) is walking distance to the morning market, the Trok Rong Ya walking street and the museum, ideal if you want to explore on foot; the Sakae Krang riverside and Ko Thepho are quiet and peaceful, where you wake up to river views — great for cycling and unwinding; and the suburbs like Tha Pho and Thap Than have resorts with pools and garden bungalows, a fit for families and self-drivers. Many people book without checking the area and end up driving back and forth all day. This guide rounds up 10 hand-picked Uthai Thani hotels across every tier — all with real guest reviews, prices compared across 3 sites and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Uthai Thani has no metro and no commercial airport — the town is compact and flat, made for self-driving and cycling, and many stays lend bicycles for free. Pick by your itinerary: the town centre (Uthai Mai) is walking distance to the riverside morning market, the Trok Rong Ya walking street and the museum, best if you want to explore on foot; the Sakae Krang riverside and Ko Thepho are quiet, where you wake to river views — great for cycling and unwinding; and the suburbs (Tha Pho·Thap Than) have resorts with pools and garden bungalows, about a 10–20 minute drive into town, handy for families and anyone driving out toward Ban Rai. Almost every stay has free parking.

entries.name: Sabua The Terrace Homestay
entries.revCount: 150 reviews · scores 9.1 · central by a lotus pond
entries.badge: 🏆 Great score, lots of reviews, walkable
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Lotus pond · town centre · walk to the walking street

entries.addr: Soi Sukkasem, Uthai Mai, Mueang Uthai Thani
entries.storyHtml: Sabua The Terrace is the garden homestay that best balances a high score with a healthy review count — 9.1 from 150 reviews. Its standout is a quiet lotus-pond garden setting right in the town centre, yet within walking distance of the Trok Rong Ya walking street and the riverside morning market. Guests praise the kind owner and consistently clean rooms; every room has a balcony over the garden or the lotus pond — a fit for anyone who wants to sleep centrally in peace while still being able to walk to the sights.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If your budget stretches, pick a room with a balcony over the lotus pond — sip a morning coffee by the water before walking to the riverside market.

entries.name: Numhom Resort

entries.mrtTag: 📍 Thap Than · between town and Ban Rai
tags: 🌿 Garden bungalows by a small pond
entries.addr: Thap Than, Thap Than District, Uthai Thani
entries.storyHtml: Numhom Resort is the most-reviewed resort in this guide — 167 reviews, scoring 9.1. Its standout is garden bungalows set in front of a small pond with a quiet country feel, plus a playground and an on-site restaurant. Parking is free right by your room and rates start at just ฿650, making it a fit for families and anyone driving out to the Ban Rai side. The trade-off is the Thap Than location — about a 20-minute drive into Uthai Thani town each time you want to hit the markets or the riverside.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Travelling as a group or family, look at the 4-bed Family Room or a One-Bedroom Bungalow in front of the pond — the per-head cost drops a lot.

entries.storyHtml: Ban Klang Gaew Resort (Baan Klang Ko) is the most-reviewed of the riverside stays — 186 reviews, scoring 8.7. Its standout is a riverside stay among the rice fields on Ko Thepho, where you wake to river and greenery views — ideal for cycling around the island morning and evening. It's about a 10–15 minute crossing from town with free parking. The trade-off is the island setting that needs a car, no shops within walking distance and no pool.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For the full effect, take the One-Bedroom House with its own sitting terrace, and borrow a bicycle to ride around Ko Thepho in the early morning before the heat.

entries.name: Sakaekrang Haven Homestay
entries.badge: 🌿 Little garden house by the river · newly opened
entries.addr: Sakae Krang, Sakae Krang riverside, Mueang Uthai Thani
entries.storyHtml: Sakaekrang Haven Homestay is a newly opened riverside homestay on the Sakae Krang scoring a high 9.0 (from 30 reviews). Its standout is a little garden house by the river within the town, with air-conditioned rooms whose balconies face the garden or the river, a calm atmosphere, an owner who runs it personally, an Asian breakfast and free parking. It's a fit for anyone who wants to sleep by the Sakae Krang in quiet and warmth. The trade-off: it's new with few reviews so far, only a handful of units, and no other meals or pool on site.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a full river view, choose the Riverside Room with a balcony facing straight out over the Sakae Krang, and book ahead as there are only a few units.

entries.name: Uthaithani Resort
tags: 🌳 Garden with a faux waterfall, photo-friendly
entries.addr: Tha Pho, Nong Khayang District, Uthai Thani
entries.storyHtml: Uthaithani Resort is the resort with a pool that suits families best in this guide, scoring 8.7 from 120 reviews. Its standout is a swimming pool with a kids' pool, a garden with a faux waterfall that photographs well, and a three-bedroom room for larger groups. Rooms are clean, parking is free, and rates start at just ฿850. It sits in the Tha Pho suburb, so you'll drive into town for every meal — but you get the pool and the extra space in return.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Travelling as a big family, look at the Three-Bedroom — the per-head cost drops — and let the kids swim in the evening before heading into town for dinner.

entries.name: Comenietee Uthai
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Old town · Uthai Mai · walk to the morning market
entries.addr: Phon Phibun Uthit Rd, old town, Uthai Mai, Mueang Uthai Thani
entries.storyHtml: Comenietee Uthai is an old wooden-house guesthouse in Uthai Thani's old town scoring a high 9.0 (from 25 reviews). Its standout is a renovated wooden house with just four warm, homely rooms, a 200-metre walk to the morning market and restaurants. Guests praise the hearty Thai breakfast and the hands-on owner; parking is free and rates start around ฿1,000. It's a fit for anyone who wants to sleep in the old town and explore on foot. The trade-off: limited rooms, some with a bathroom outside the room, and none of the facilities of a larger hotel.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Few rooms and a high score mean it fills fast on long weekends — book ahead. For an en-suite bathroom, pick the Queen or Superior at booking.

entries.name: TJ Boutique Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Wongsa Rot Rd · Uthai Mai · near the town market
entries.addr: Wongsa Rot Rd, Uthai Mai, Mueang Uthai Thani
entries.storyHtml: TJ Boutique Hotel is a small in-town boutique run hands-on by the owner, with 150 reviews and a focus on cleanliness, scoring 8.4. Its standout is the owner-led service: air-conditioned rooms of about 22 sqm, each with a private balcony and a fridge, and guests single out the cleanliness in particular. There's free parking, free bikes to borrow and breakfast served to your room. It sits on Wongsa Rot Road near the town market, from around ฿1,000. The trade-off: limited rooms and no restaurant for other meals on site.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Borrow a hotel bicycle and ride along the Sakae Krang River in the early morning or evening — the prettiest time to take in Uthai Thani.

entries.addr: Soi Na Thong, Uthai Mai, Mueang Uthai Thani
entries.storyHtml: Shon Boutique is a newly opened in-town boutique in an English-garden style that stands out for cleanliness and being pet-friendly, scoring 8.6 from its early reviews. Its standout is a low building wrapped around an English-garden-meets-minimalist garden, with fresh-looking rooms, strong hot water, on-site parking and a buffet breakfast. Tucked into Soi Na Thong near the provincial court, it's quiet, from around ฿900 during promotions. The trade-off: it's newly opened with few reviews, and standard rooms are fairly compact — groups should ask for the Family Room.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: As a new stay, some periods run a promo from ฿900 including breakfast — message their page before booking. Notify them in advance if bringing a pet.

entries.name: PaeStay
entries.revCount: 24 reviews · floating raft house on the Sakae Krang
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Sakae Krang riverside · town centre · 200 m to the morning market
tags: 🚶 200 m to the riverside morning market
entries.addr: Pae Khlong Sakae Krang Rd, Uthai Mai, Mueang Uthai Thani
entries.storyHtml: PaeStay is the pick for anyone who wants to try sleeping on a floating raft house on the Sakae Krang River for a night, scoring 7.4 from 24 reviews. Its standout is the one-of-a-kind experience — a real floating wooden raft, vintage-style rooms with balconies over the river, and a spot just 200 metres from the riverside morning market, an easy walk for breakfast. It's a way to soak up the riverside life right in the centre of Uthai Thani. The trade-off: raft-house rooms are simple, the Standard shares a bathroom, and online reviews are still few.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For an en-suite bathroom and the full river-view balcony, step up to a Deluxe or above. Waking early to walk to the riverside morning market just 200 m away is the highlight.

faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Uthai Thani hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area is best to stay in Uthai Thani?
faq.a: It depends on your itinerary and whether you have a car. The town centre (Uthai Mai) is walkable to the riverside morning market, the Trok Rong Ya walking street and the museum, best for exploring on foot (Sabua The Terrace, Comenietee Uthai, TJ Boutique, Shon Boutique, PaeStay). The Sakae Krang riverside and Ko Thepho are quiet, great for cycling and unwinding (Sakaekrang Haven, Ban Klang Gaew). The suburbs (Tha Pho·Thap Than) have resorts with pools and garden bungalows, a fit for families and self-drivers (Uthaithani Resort, Numhom Resort).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Uthai Thani hotels cost?
faq.a: Uthai Thani is friendly on the wallet: bungalows and budget stays start around ฿650–800 (Numhom Resort, C2U Hotel); 3-star resorts and boutiques run about ฿850–1,200 (Uthaithani Resort, Ban Klang Gaew, TJ Boutique, Sabua The Terrace); riverside homestays and a raft house run from about ฿1,200 (Sakaekrang Haven, PaeStay). Prices move with the date and the season.

faq.q: ❓ Where should I stay to be on the Sakae Krang River?
faq.a: To wake up to Sakae Krang River views: Sakaekrang Haven Homestay ฿1,200 is a little garden house by the river within town, scoring 9.0; Ban Klang Gaew Resort ฿900 is a riverside stay on Ko Thepho, good for cycling around the island; or for something unusual, try PaeStay ฿1,200, a floating raft house near the riverside morning market.

faq.q: ❓ Which Uthai Thani hotel has a swimming pool?
faq.a: In this guide the one with a pool is Uthaithani Resort ฿850, a Tha Pho resort with a swimming pool and a kids' pool, a photo-friendly faux-waterfall garden, and a three-bedroom room for big families — a good fit for groups.

faq.q: ❓ Is it easy to get around Uthai Thani without a car?
faq.a: Uthai Thani has no metro, but the town is compact and flat. If you stay in the centre (Uthai Mai) you can walk to the morning market, the walking street and the Sakae Krang riverside. Many stays lend bikes for free — for example TJ Boutique Hotel — so cycling along the river and around town is easy. But for Thap Than, Tha Pho or Ko Thepho, a car is much smoother.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Uthai Thani hotel?
faq.a: On normal weekdays, 1–2 weeks ahead is enough as Uthai Thani isn't crowded. But on long weekends and holidays, small-room stays like the homestays Sabua The Terrace, Comenietee Uthai and Sakaekrang Haven fill very fast, so book 2–4 weeks ahead or more.
